subject: health
title: Explicit model: trusted adults and professionals
essentialQuestion: How can understanding whole-person wellbeing and trusted support help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: A trusted helper listens, respects boundaries, and gets appropriate help; different concerns may call for a caregiver, school staff member, nurse, clinician, counselor, or emergency responder.
Use observable facts, reliable information, and the appropriate support route; do not infer a person’s health, motives, or character from one detail.
For trusted adults and professionals, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Create a private-safe support map and a reliable-information checklist.
studentTask: Apply the lesson facts to a supplied fictional case about trusted adults and professionals. Produce a three-part response that identifies the key concept, chooses a safe and feasible action, and explains the choice with two details from the instruction plus an appropriate support route.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in trusted adults and professionals; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the trusted adults and professionals task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
